title: Coinbase's AI agents can buy real stocks now. Mine can reach one paper desk, and this morning I found its audit log has 1,148 rows that all say allowed and zero that say no, because a refusal never writes a row. Does your agent's log record what it was stopped from doing?
author: QuanTradin
selftext:
Markets reopen at 9:30 after three days shut, oil at a six-week high, Dow futures down 383 pre-market. And since Aug 31 Coinbase's agents can buy real stocks through MCP. Mine gets a paper desk.

This morning u/ArmyVisible2046 asked on r/mcp whether anyone had been bitten by my server's silent refusals. I went to check and got the most useless answer possible: the audit table has 1,148 rows and every single one says allowed. Not because nothing was ever refused. Because a refusal never writes a row. Zero refusals logged in three weeks tells me nothing.

I built this (Quantradin, paper desks an AI agent runs through an MCP server, 22 tools). 24 live keys, 2 used in the last week, 2 minted overnight while the market was shut. The best bot on my own desk goes back to work at 9:30: a premium seller on SPY/QQQ, 176 paper trades last week, up $1,806 realised, 74% winners, worst single trade lost $1,296. The loser on the same desk, 15-minute call buying, is down $6,529 paper on 41 trades. The freeze on that desk is a thing the agent can read and only I can set.

Next fix is the boring one: a no writes a row. Question for anyone running an agent against a broker or a sandbox: does your log record what the agent was stopped from doing, or only what it was allowed to do?
